header: Date: 2027-05-10 15:00 PDT | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Sam Torres (Redwood AE), Priya Karthik (Redwood SE), John Malik (Mosaic CTO), Elena Ruiz (Head of ML), Marcus Chen (Infra) | Recorded: yes
transcript:
[00:00] Sam Torres: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Sam, i'm the AE on the account. Quick roll call?
[00:07] John Malik: John here, CTO at Mosaic.
[00:09] Elena Ruiz: Elena, head of ML.
[00:11] Marcus Chen: Marcus, infra.
[00:13] Priya Karthik: Priya, solutions engineer at Redwood.
[00:15] Sam Torres: Awesome, thanks. Goal for today is a quick walkthrough of structured output / JSON mode and function calling, show how we enforce schemas and guardrails, and then demo a short pilot plan. We'll leave time for Q&A.
[00:30] John Malik: Sounds good. We're particularly interested in reliable JSON responses for our product catalog generator and the ability to call downstream tools to upsert items.
[00:38] Elena Ruiz: Also want to see how strict the schema enforcement is - we had a bunch of hallucinated fields with another provider.
[00:45] Priya Karthik: Totally, we'll show both soft and hard schema enforcement, validation and auto-correct suggestions. We'll also show a function-calling flow that writes back to a mock inventory API.
[00:55] Sam Torres: Quick context: Mosaic is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private. You'll want predictable latency for catalog updates during peak ingest windows, and data residency / audit for compliance.
[01:05] Marcus Chen: Yep, and we need to know if we can run this inside our VPC, or if we have to use Redwood Dedicated with private networking.
[01:13] Priya Karthik: We have both options. Private gives you VPC control plane and on-prem packages if needed. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with SLA. We'll add notes on IP allowlist and KMS options in the security packet.
[01:25] Sam Torres: Alright, demo time. Priya, take it away.
[01:28] Priya Karthik: Sure. I'm going to start in the API mode - JSON mode. We'll show the prompt + schema, then the Console where you can set guardrails at the route level.
[01:40] [01:40] Priya Karthik: (screen) First step - we define a JSON schema for product items: sku (string), title (string), price (number), categories (array of strings), availability {status, qty}, and metadata. We add required fields and a regex for sku.
[01:58] Elena Ruiz: What happens if the model outputs price as a string or misses qty?
[02:03] Priya Karthik: Two modes: soft validation - we return the output plus a validation report and suggestions; hard validation - the runtime enforces schema and will reject or attempt structured-corrected output. Example: price: '29.99' will be coerced to 29.99 in auto-coerce mode; missing required fields fail the call unless you allow partial returns.
[02:23] John Malik: Who owns the correction logic? Is it Redwood or the model?
[02:27] Priya Karthik: It's a combination. The runtime runs a deterministic validator against the schema post-generation and applies safe coercions we define. You can plug custom validators or run an eval hook to review changes.
[02:36] Marcus Chen: Any perf hit on strict validation? We care about p99 latency.
[02:40] Priya Karthik: Minimal. The validator is lightweight and runs in-process. In our internal profiling we see <1-3 ms additional per request for typical schemas; worst case if you run heavy custom validators it can add more. We'll include a micro-benchmark in the pilot.
[02:55] [03:00] Priya Karthik: Now function calling: here's an example where the model returns a structured JSON and a function signature that maps to an inventory_update endpoint. The runtime can auto-call the function (tool) or return the payload for your app to call.
[03:15] Sam Torres: We'll demo both modes. Auto-call with safe-mode on - we have guardrails so calls that touch PII or billing flows require manual approval.
[03:25] Elena Ruiz: How do you prevent unauthorized function calls, like calling arbitrary endpoints?
[03:30] Priya Karthik: Each function is registered with the route and has an allowlist. The runtime only exposes registered function schemas. You can also set RBAC and token scopes per function so only certain roles can enable auto-call.
[03:42] John Malik: Can we see the audit log for function calls?
[03:45] Priya Karthik: Yes - Console shows a trace for every call: input, model output, function payload, execution response, and who triggered it. Those logs can be routed to your SIEM or retained per your retention policy.
[03:56] Marcus Chen: Good. What's the max payload size to the function? Our inventory API expects the full product blob with images sometimes.
[04:03] Priya Karthik: We recommend keeping structured payloads focused (metadata + image URLs). For large binaries we store references and use your internal blob store. Function payload max default is 1 MB; can be extended in Dedicated/Private. We'll check your image flow in the pilot.
[04:18] [04:20] Priya Karthik: Demo: sending a prompt to create a product from a short description. Model returns: {"sku":"MOSA-1299","title":"Everyday Running Shoe","price":89.99,"categories":["shoes","running"],"availability":{"status":"in_stock","qty":120}}. Then the runtime maps that to inventory_update(sku, payload) and auto-calls.
[04:42] John Malik: That output looks clean. Any chance of hallucinated categories?
[04:45] Priya Karthik: We run category normalization via a second step - post-process rule that maps free-text categories to canonical taxonomy. You can provide the taxonomy file to Console so normalization happens automatically.
[04:56] Elena Ruiz: If the model is uncertain it should ask clarifying question instead of guessing.
[04:59] Priya Karthik: We have a 'clarify' flow: when the model's probability/confidence for required fields falls below a threshold, the runtime will return a clarifying prompt to the user or to a human-in-the-loop queue.
[05:12] Sam Torres: Let's switch to Console and show route-level guardrails.
[05:16] [05:16] Priya Karthik: (screen) In Console you can create a route -> attach a schema -> add pre/post validators -> set function allowlist -> enable auto-call or manual review -> set rollout (canary %) and fallback model.
[05:30] Marcus Chen: Can you set concurrency or batching per route?
[05:33] Priya Karthik: Yes, route config includes batch window, max tokens, and autoscaling policies for Dedicated. Optimize will also suggest batching and quantization settings based on observed seq length distribution.
[05:44] John Malik: About Optimize - can it recommend quantization profiles that won't degrade our catalog classification accuracy?
[05:49] Priya Karthik: Optimize runs a quick eval against your labeled prompt set and shows tradeoffs: latency, cost, and quality delta. You can pin a quality threshold and the optimizer suggests the tightest quantization that meets it.
[05:59] Elena Ruiz: We'll need the eval harness and sample prompts.
[06:02] Sam Torres: We'll include a template prompt set in the follow-up materials.
[06:06] [06:10] John Malik: Security - we need full KMS integration. How's key custody handled?
[06:14] Priya Karthik: We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations in Dedicated and Private. In hosted, we offer envelope encryption and can integrate with your KMS for key wrapping. Full key control is available in Private on-prem.
[06:28] Marcus Chen: Audit logs retention and export?
[06:30] Priya Karthik: Configurable per deployment; we can push logs to your S3 or SIEM. We'll share our SOC 2 and ISO docs.
[06:38] John Malik: Latency numbers - what p99 for a structured create (short seq)?
[06:42] Priya Karthik: For hosted with our small models we typically see p50 ~ 30-50 ms, p95 ~ 120-200 ms; with Dedicated reserved GPUs you can get p95 << 100 ms depending on model. We'll run your pilot to profile under your seq lengths.
[06:58] Elena Ruiz: Cost - what's the delta when you enable strict validation and function-calling?
[07:02] Priya Karthik: Minor compute overhead for validation. The bigger cost is model tokens + function execution. Optimize recommendations can cut token cost via caching templates and prefix caching. We'll propose a pilot with estimated unit economics.
[07:18] [07:20] Priya Karthik: Live example of guardrail kicking in: I intentionally send a prompt missing 'sku' and switch on hard validation; runtime rejects and returns an error with a structured validation report suggesting sku candidates.
[07:34] John Malik: Could that block our ingestion pipeline? We have batch jobs that expect always-success.
[07:38] Sam Torres: You can configure fallback: on validation fail, either write to DLQ for manual review, fallback to a permissive model, or auto-fill certain fields using deterministic rules.
[07:48] Marcus Chen: What's the DLQ integration - SQS? Kafka?
[07:50] Priya Karthik: We support push to SQS, Kafka, Pub/Sub, or you can have a webhook to your internal pipeline.
[07:59] Elena Ruiz: Regarding taxonomy normalization, will that be part of Redwood or our service?
[08:03] Priya Karthik: Either. We can host a normalization table and run it in the runtime, or the runtime can return normalized tags and you can enforce them on write.
[08:13] John Malik: Can we restrict which models are used per route? We want to limit generative models to curated verified ones.
[08:17] Priya Karthik: Yes - route-level model whitelist. You can also pin to a model family and allow Redwood fallback options only within that whitelist.
[08:27] Sam Torres: Quick note on function calling safety: we log function schemas and the runtime refuses to call any unregistered function even if the model output includes a function name.
[08:37] John Malik: Good. Last question on SLAs and commitment windows - what's minimum for Dedicated?
[08:41] Sam Torres: Typically 6-12 month reserved capacity commits; we'll share exact tiers in follow-up.
[08:47] [08:50] Priya Karthik: Ok, switching to a short end-to-end flow: Prompt -> Model -> Schema validation -> FunctionCall(inventory_update) -> Response. I'll trigger auto-call.
[09:00] [09:05] (model) Generated payload with price as '89.99' string; runtime coerced to number, normalized category 'running' -> 'Athletics > Running Shoes', and auto-called inventory_update. Function returned 200 OK with internal id.
[09:20] Elena Ruiz: Nice, can we see the audit trace?
[09:22] Priya Karthik: (screen) Trace shows input prompt, tokens sampled, schema validation diff (coerced price, normalized categories), function payload and response, and role-based user who authorized auto-call.
[09:36] John Malik: This looks promising. For the pilot, we want: 1) 10k records ingestion run with 95th p99 reporting 2) Schema enforcement tests 3) Function-calling end-to-end writes to a sandbox inventory 4) Cost estimate.
[09:52] Sam Torres: That's exactly what we'll run. Priya, can you own the bench?
[09:56] Priya Karthik: Yep, i'll spin up a quick bench and share results within a week.
[10:01] Marcus Chen: One more infra note: we need IP allowlist and VPC peering for the sandbox.
[10:04] Sam Torres: We'll coordinate with your infra team. Marcus, can you send the CIDR ranges?
[10:08] Marcus Chen: Will do.
[10:10] John Malik: Alright, final recap please.
[10:12] Sam Torres: Recap: Redwood demoed JSON structured output + function calling with guardrails. Action items: Sam share recording + docs; Priya run 10k ingestion pilot and bench schema and function-calls; Mosaic to provide sample schema + CIDR ranges. We'll also send SOC 2 and KMS notes and pricing.
[10:30] Elena Ruiz: Thanks, folks.
[10:32] Sam Torres: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot start.
[10:35] (call ends)
